target: Only the extra outer bracts are absent: the small bracts at the base of the involucre, or on the peduncle (PO:0009053). Record bracteole PO:0009043 or bract PO:0009055 with context 'outer, at base of involucre' as absent (PATO:0000462). The involucral bracts (PO:0009045) are present and villous
fix: In Asteraceae, 'involucre not bracteate', 'not calyculate', 'ecalyculate' and 'without outer bracts' deny only the outer extra bracts below the involucre. They are never 'bract absent' or 'involucral bract absent' for the whole taxon.
reason: Every Sinosenecio head has involucral bracts. 'Not bracteate' is the usual FOC phrase for an involucre with no outer bracts.

target: Leaf (PO:0025034) is absent along the flowering stem (PO:0009047) except at its apex, where the leaves are crowded (subrosulate). Keep 'except at apex' or 'lower and middle part of stem' as the context
fix: 'leafless except at apex', 'leafless except at base' and 'leaves only at X' say where the leaves sit. Record the leaves as present at X and keep the position as the context. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf absent'.
reason: The same stem is bare below and leafy at the top. The rosette statement describes those top leaves.

target: Bracteole PO:0009043 absent (PATO:0000462). The bract (PO:0009055) at the base of the peduncle is present and subulate
fix: 'not bracteolate', 'ebracteolate' and 'without bracteoles' map to bracteole PO:0009043. They never map to bract PO:0009055, even though the bract term lists 'bracteole' as a synonym.
reason: The text has both a basal subulate bract and no bracteoles. These are different organs.

target: Lower glume PO:0006002 absent (PATO:0000462). Upper glume PO:0006004 lanceolate
fix: 'lower glume absent', 'first glume absent' and 'lower glume suppressed' map to lower glume PO:0006002. 'Upper glume ...' maps to upper glume PO:0006004. Neither goes to the general term glume PO:0009039.
reason: Zoysia is known for having no lower glume and a well-developed upper glume.

target: Nothing is absent, so drop the absence record. The sentence is about specialized asexual propagules, which were not observed, and has nothing to do with leaves. The subulate leaf annotation can stay
fix: '<structure> not seen', 'not observed' and 'not known' report a gap in the material. They are never an absence. Also, a 'not seen' sentence must never be annotated to a part that it does not name.
reason: Dicranum has leaves. The absence statement does not mention leaves.

target: Stipel PO:0020051 absent (PATO:0000462). The stipules (PO:0020041) are present and slender
fix: 'stipelle(s)' (French), 'stipel(s)' and 'estipellate' map to stipel PO:0020051, never to stipule PO:0020041.
reason: Stipels are the small stipule-like parts at the base of leaflets. Tephrosia has stipules but no stipels.

target: Style (PO:0009074) absent in the ray flowers (PO:0025331), which are neuter. The disk flowers (PO:0025332) have a style. Keep 'ray flower' or 'disk flower' as the context, and check whether 'glabre' refers to the style at all
fix: In Asteraceae, 'style absent' or 'styles nuls' inside a ray-floret sentence apply only to the ray flowers. Keep the floret type as the context and never record 'style absent' for the whole taxon.
reason: Aspilia has sterile ray florets with no style and fertile disk florets with a style. Since 'glabre' carries no part name, the style annotation itself may also be wrong.

target: Bract (PO:0009055) is absent only on the outside of the fig (around the ostiole or on its wall; context 'external'). The 2–3 basal bracts at the base of the fig are present and small. Keep 'external/ostiolar' and 'basal' as the context
fix: In Ficus, 'sans bractées externes', 'without lateral bracts' and 'without external bracts' deny only the bracts on the fig wall or at the ostiole. They never deny the basal bracts. Keep the position as the context.
reason: Ficus figs normally have basal bracts and may lack lateral or external ones. The two statements are about different groups of bracts.

target: Bract (PO:0009055) with context 'external, at the ostiole' absent. The basal bracts of the fig persist (bract with context 'basal'). Check that 'à bases persistantes' really describes bracts
fix: In Ficus, 'ostiole sans bractées externes' refers to the ostiolar bracts visible from outside. Record the absence with the context 'ostiole, external', and never as 'bract absent' for the whole taxon.
reason: The ostiole statement is about the bracts at the top of the fig. The persistent bracts are elsewhere.

target: Stipel PO:0020051 absent (PATO:0000462). The stipules (PO:0020041) are present and acute
fix: 'sans stipelles', 'stipelles nulles' and 'estipellate' map to stipel PO:0020051, never to stipule PO:0020041.
reason: The absence is about stipels on the leaflets. The stipules are described.

target: Bract (PO:0009055) is absent only on the side of the fig (context 'lateral'). The basal bracts are present and whorled (context 'basal')
fix: In Ficus, 'without lateral bracts' denies only the bracts on the fig wall. 'Basal bracts ... verticillate' describes other bracts. Keep 'lateral' or 'basal' as the context.
reason: Ficus descriptions routinely give lateral and basal bracts separately.

target: Cystoliths are absent from the leaf lamina. Record idioblast PO:0000283 (the cell type that holds cystoliths) with context 'cystolith' as absent (PATO:0000462), on leaf lamina PO:0020039. The lamina itself is present, with a dentate margin
fix: 'cystoliths absent', 'domatia absent', 'dots absent', 'glands absent' and 'hairs absent' said of a part deny a structure on that part, never the part itself. Record the structure as the bearer, with the part as the context.
reason: A leaf with a dentate margin cannot lack a lamina. Only the cystoliths in it are missing.

target: Trichome PO:0000282 absent (PATO:0000462) on the inner surface of the fig (context 'internal'). The fruit (PO:0009001) is present
fix: 'internal hairs absent', 'interfloral hairs absent' and 'hairs inside absent' (Ficus) map to trichome PO:0000282 with context 'inside the fig'. They never map to fruit absent.
reason: The sentence is about hairs inside the fig, not about the fig.

target: Bract (PO:0009055) with context 'lateral, on the fig wall' absent (PATO:0000462). The fruit (PO:0009001) is present with a convex apex
fix: In Ficus, 'without lateral bracts' maps to bract with context 'lateral'. It never maps to fruit absent, whatever the heading of the sentence.
reason: A part named in the phrase ('bracts') was replaced by the sentence's heading ('fruit').

target: Nothing is absent. The bracts (PO:0009055) are caducous (falling early), which is why they were not seen. Keep only the deciduous annotation
fix: 'not seen', 'not observed' and 'caducous, not seen' report a gap in the material. They are never an absence. When 'caducous' is in the same sentence, record only the deciduous quality.
reason: Bracts that fall early are present at first but missing from the specimens.

target: The leaf lamina (PO:0020039) has no dots; punctate (PATO:0001512) does not apply. The leaf is present. Drop the absence, or record it as 'not punctate' if the negation is supported
fix: 'dots absent', 'without dots', 'not punctate' and 'epunctate' describe the leaf surface (no gland dots). They are never 'leaf absent'.
reason: In Myristicaceae, keys often mention dots on the lower leaf surface. A papillate lower surface shows the leaf is present.

target: The leaf lamina (PO:0020039) is not punctate (punctate PATO:0001512 negated). The lamina is present and pale greenish yellow below
fix: 'dots absent' and 'without dots' are a surface quality of the lamina (not punctate). They are never 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: Same Myristicaceae wording as X02505. The lamina is described.

target: Nothing is absent. Stipules (PO:0020041) are deciduous; the 'not seen' part only explains why they are missing from the specimens
fix: 'caducous, not seen' and 'early caducous, not seen' mean present but falling early. Record the deciduous quality only, never an absence.
reason: One sentence produced both records. 'Not seen' is a gap in the material, not an absence.

target: Cauline leaf PO:0000013 absent on the flowering stem or scape (PO:0009047). The basal leaves are present
fix: 'without leaves' or 'leafless' said of a scape or flowering stem refers to the cauline leaves only, never to all leaves.
reason: Heuchera has a basal rosette and leafless or nearly leafless scapes.

target: Ray flower PO:0025331 absent (PATO:0000462). The flowers (PO:0009046), which are disk flowers (PO:0025332), are present. The heads are arranged in lax terminal corymbs
fix: 'ray florets absent', 'rays absent', 'eradiate' and 'discoid' map to ray flower PO:0025331, never to flower PO:0009046.
reason: Emilia heads are discoid: they have disk flowers only.

target: The fruit (PO:0009001) has no apical peg (beak). Record the peg, with context 'apical peg', as absent on the fruit apex. The fruit itself is present
fix: 'apical peg absent', 'beak absent' and 'without a stipe' deny a feature of the fruit. Record the feature as the bearer, or a negated shape of the fruit apex, never 'fruit absent'.
reason: A purple-pink fruit is described. Only the small apical projection is missing.

target: Leaf (PO:0025034) is present but few and of decreased size (PATO:0000587), reduced to scales (scale leaf PO:0006003). Nothing is absent
fix: 'nearly leafless', 'subaphyllous' and 'almost leafless' qualify a quantity. They are never an absence. 'Reduced to scales' maps to scale leaf PO:0006003 or decreased size.
reason: Both statements say the leaves are much reduced. Neither says they are absent.

target: Domatia are absent from the leaf lamina (PO:0020039); domatium has no PO class, so record it as context 'domatia' or propose a FLOPO anatomy class. The lamina is present
fix: 'domatia absent' and 'without domatia' deny small pockets in the vein angles under the leaf. They are never 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: Rubiaceae floras routinely state whether domatia are present. The lamina is described.

target: Leaf lamina (PO:0020039) is absent only in the lower leaves, which are bladeless basal sheaths (scale leaf PO:0006003 or leaf sheath PO:0020104). The upper leaves have thin blades. Keep 'lower leaves' as the context
fix: In Carex and other sedges, 'the lower bladeless' and 'lower sheaths bladeless' apply to the basal sheaths only. Keep 'lower or basal' as the context, or map them to scale leaf PO:0006003. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: Sedges often have bladeless sheaths at the base and normal blades above.

target: The basal leaves are bladeless sheaths: scale leaf PO:0006003 (or leaf sheath PO:0020104 with context 'basal'). The leaf lamina of the normal leaves is present and flat
fix: 'reduced to bladeless sheaths' and 'bladeless sheaths' map to scale leaf PO:0006003 for the basal leaves. They are never 'leaf lamina absent' (this is the main error in the moss flora check of docs/km-classification.md).
reason: The flat blades belong to the normal leaves. The sheaths are the lowest leaves.

target: 'Axis stout' is the inflorescence axis PO:0020122 (or peduncle PO:0009053), not the stem. Stemless means the plant has a very short stem with crowded leaves (acaulescent); it does not mean stem absent
fix: In Bromeliaceae and in rosette plants, 'axis', 'primary axis' and 'rachis' inside an inflorescence description map to inflorescence axis PO:0020122. 'Stemless' and 'acaulescent' mean the stem is very short, never 'stem absent'.
reason: The flora's word 'axis' belongs to the inflorescence. The stem record took it from the stem synonym list ('primary axis').

target: Nothing is absent: the capsules were not collected. Drop the fruit absence. Check where 'with acute apex' comes from: if no fruit was seen, it probably describes another part (a leaf or the perianth lobe)
fix: 'capsules not seen', 'fruits unknown' and 'fruit not seen' report a gap in the material. They are never an absence. When a flora says the fruit was not seen, no fruit quality should be annotated.
reason: Aristolochia has capsules. A new species described without fruits cannot have a fruit shape.

target: Glume (PO:0009039) awnless: awn (PO:0025349) absent on the glumes. The lemma awn (PO:0006032) is present and dorsal
fix: In GrassBase, 'muticous' belongs to the organ that the sentence is about (glumes, upper glume, sterile lemma, and so on). Attach the awn absence to that organ, never to awn for the whole taxon.
reason: Alopecurus has awnless glumes and a dorsally awned lemma. GrassBase lists them in separate sentences.

target: Palea (PO:0009038) is absent or reduced only in the sterile florets (context 'sterile or rudimentary floret'). The fertile florets have a palea with scabrous keels
fix: In GrassBase, 'without significant palea' appears in the sentence on sterile or rudimentary florets. Keep the floret type as the context and never record 'palea absent' for the whole taxon.
reason: The fertile florets of Elymus have a well-developed palea, so the absence must refer to other florets.

target: Trichome PO:0000282 absent (PATO:0000462) on the leaf, which is the same as leaf glabrous (PATO:0000453). The leaf (PO:0025034) is present and furrowed
fix: A heading of the form 'Hairs: absent' or 'Trichomes: absent' maps to trichome PO:0000282, with the section's part as the context. It is never '<part> absent'.
reason: The absence is about the hairs. The leaf is described as furrowed.
